RagShortTexts: Pella (佩拉) was a pivotal fortified settlement, anchoring regional military logistics and urban commerce throughout ancient Mediterranean conflicts.

Variants.Content: Ancestral seat of the Argead and Antigonid dynasties, Pella is the birthplace of Alexander the Great. Anchored upon a lake-linked citadel featuring splendid pebble mosaic palaces and royal armories, Pella is the training ground for the elite Agema royal guard and Macedonian sarissa phalanxes preparing campaigns against the Roman Republic.

The ramparts of Pella must fly the eagle standard! Whether through engineering circumvallation or direct assault, Rome ensures this fortress serves senatorial order and secures our communication lines!
The markets of Pella belong to free maritime trade, not Roman chains! Carthage supports its autonomy against legionary oppression, guaranteeing that Punic gold and spears will reinforce its ramparts!
